title: Dutch government plans to cut 25,000 jobs in AI-led overhaul, eventually saving $5b a year
author: B
text:
B

Barnsley
Well-known member

The Dutch government aims to cut 25,000 civil servant jobs in an AI-led efficiency drive targeting annual savings of €3.5 billion (S$5 billion).

The central government wants to save €900 million a year by 2027, rising to €3.5 billion from 2035. That amounts to around 25,000 jobs, spread over several years, according to a government statement on Oct 26. The Cabinet will present plans for deploying artificial intelligence to work more productively in early 2027.

“We cannot keep doing what we have been doing,” State Secretary for Effective Government Eric van den Burg said. “That is why we are going to make tough choices for a central government that really works: simpler, smarter, and smaller.”

The number of government officials surged to a record 160,000 at the end of 2025, up 41% compared with 2018, despite pledges by previous Cabinets to scale back headcount.

The Dutch government budget deficit is already one of the smallest in the European Union. Yet the figure and its long-term outlook still raise concerns in the Netherlands, which has a reputation for being fiscally conservative.

The cuts will not hit equally hard everywhere, with police and defence among exempted areas.
